text:
sam: Sketching a decision graph for tenant routing. Want to account for data-residency tags, explicit consent flags, active-active preferences, and an operator override matrix. Sharing a rough ASCII sketch — feedback? :thinking:

sam: ```
start -> check residency_tag
  -> if EU -> prefer eu-primary
  -> else -> check consent_flag
    -> if no_transfer -> local-only
    -> else -> evaluate(latency, cost_delta)
      -> if latency < 120ms and cost_delta < 1.2 -> nearest-region
      -> else -> tiered-fallback (dedicated -> hosted)
```

mara: I like the explicit consent short-circuit. Question: how do we encode "local-only" for tenants that still want low-latency reads but can't leave region? Do we allow cross-region read replicas that only cache non-PII?

lee: Two quick thoughts: 1) we need a tag "cacheable_by_policy" on datasets, otherwise we risk leaking PII. 2) operator overrides should be auditable and surface a reason code. Maybe `override:{actor,reason,expires_at}`

olivia: +1 on auditable overrides. For the decision graph, can we add a cost budget check early? Some tenants have strict cost caps and should never escalate to dedicated if cost would blow the monthly commit.

sam: Good call. Proposed order update: residency -> consent -> cost_budget_check -> latency/cost tradeoff. If budget exhausted -> signal operator + route to best-effort hosted with notice.

mara: Edge case: active-active with split-write (two regions accept writes). If tenant residency = EU but we prefer nearest for latency, do we allow EU tenant to write to US standby for latency spikes? My instinct: never for writes unless token-level consent present. We should encode write_policy: STRICT_RESIDENCY | ALLOW_ESCROW_WRITE.

lee: Agree. Reads can be relaxed if `data_class == non_pii && cacheable_by_policy`. Writes must follow write_policy. Also: add a probe step that validates downstream KMS region match before returning success when writing across regions.

sam: Draft operator override matrix idea: [override_code]: {scope, allowed_until, requires_2fa, reason_choices}. Example: `OVR-RECHECK-24h: {scope:tenant, allowed_until:24h, requires_2fa:true, reason_choices:["emergency_failover","cost_blitz"]}`

devops-bot: deploy-checklist: remember to add telemetry for `decision_node` and `final_routing_reason` (string), and emit `override_audit` on any manual action.

olivia: We should also record the decision graph version id in the request path so we can replay and repro the routing decisions for audits (e.g., `X-Routing-Graph: v2026-03-01-1`).

sam: Action items: 1) I'll update the graph with cost_budget_check and write_policy nodes. 2) @lee please draft a small schema for `override` audit events. 3) @mara please propose how to mark datasets `cacheable_by_policy`. 4) @olivia can you stub the header versioning on the proxy side?

mara: Will do. Quick note: add a fallback bucket for tenants with mixed requirements so we don't oscillate between policies during transient spikes. Maybe a 5-minute sticky decision.

lee: +1 on sticky window. Also recommend a simple simulation harness: 1) feed synthetic tenants with mixed flags 2) simulate region outage 3) measure policy thrash and operator alerts.

sam: Nice. I'll open an RFC follow-up with the updated graph and a short simulation plan. Thanks all :thumbsup:
